title: Console landscape & hierarchy synthesis (notes, wireframes, backlog)
content:
Context and goal:

This note collects synthesis from the Nov->Feb IA sprint: multiple sketch reviews, user session clips, and the early grooming sessions that attempted to move from a large list-based sidebar to a domain-first, task-oriented surface. Goal: land a minimal hierarchy that reduces cognitive plumbing for new users, enables predictable deep-linking for integrators, and makes rollout incremental (no big-bang restructure).

Constraints and non-goals:
- Must preserve existing public deep links (back-compat).
- Keep Console stable for Dedicated/Private customers during rollout (feature flag gated).
- Non-goal: global redesign of all page chrome — iterate in vertical slices.

Summary of proposal (high level):
1) Surface zones: instead of a single dense sidebar, split the console into four top-level zones: Global Topbar (account + org switcher + quick actions), Primary Hub Rail (persona/task entrypoints), Workspace Strip (contextual header for project/model/route), and Surface Modules (main content, tool panels).
2) Hub-first routing: primary routes map to user intent (Explore, Deploy, Monitor, Optimize, Admin). Secondary routes are workspace-scoped and expressed as path fragments (/hub/:hubId/... or /org/:orgId/workspace/:wsId/...).
3) Deep-link contract: canonical route schema and migration plan so external customers and docs can depend on stable URLs. Provide redirect middleware for legacy paths.

Why this is different than earlier drafts:
- Focuses on "task hub" semantics instead of flat feature lists. This reduces overlap where users search both "models" and "deploys" for the same flow.
- Adds an explicit Workspace Strip to contain context-level controls (active model, pinned prompt set, route selector) rather than hiding them in page-level headers.
- Emphasizes incremental rollout with feature flags + redirect map so we can A/B test route density.

Wireframe notes (quick sketches mapped to zones):
- Hub Rail (left, collapsible): 5-7 primary hubs (icons + label), compact mode shows icons only. Hover expands with micro-copy. Hubs prioritized by usage (telemetry-guided).
- Workspace strip (top of surface): breadcrumb-like chips: [Org] > [Workspace] > [Model: llama-3-8k] > [Route: default]. Each chip opens a focused popover for quick context switches.
- Surface modules: split-view panels (center content + right-side tools). Tools can be pinned; when the workspace changes, pinned tools persist.
- Mobile / narrow: Hub as bottom sheet, workspace strip becomes a single context pill + chevron.

Routing & path examples (canonical):
- /hub/explore -> hub-level landing (models, templates, evaluation quickstarts)
- /hub/deploy -> deploy flow index (create, draft, history)
- /org/rdw-internal/workspace/123/model/llama-3-8k/route/default -> workspace-scoped route view (model + route + config)

Legacy compatibility plan:
- Redirect table service to map old routes -> new canonical routes. Start with high-traffic pages (top 20 by usage). Ticket: CONSOLE-8123.
- Middleware returns 301 initially, then once stable also surface in the console nav as legacy aliases for one release.

Access control and onboarding states:
- Nav should be permission-aware: hubs visible per role (e.g., Audit hub only for org-admins). Use an adaptive affordance: unavailable hubs greyed with CTA to request access.
- Onboarding banner for new orgs: contextual task list in Hub Rail (first-run flows pinned).

Telemetry and analytics (what we must track):
- Hub click, hub expand/compact toggle, workspace-switch, deep-link landing path, redirect middleware hits, 404s from legacy links, time-to-first-action after landing.
- Instrumentation events: nav.hub_click, nav.workspace_switch, nav.context_popover_open, nav.legacy_redirect. Attach user properties: org_id, workspace_id, role, plan_tier.

Accessibility and keyboard focus rules:
- Hub rail must be keyboard navigable with clear focus states; space/enter to open, arrow keys to traverse micro-menus.
- Breadcrumb chips are buttons with aria-expanded where relevant.

Backlog grooming (sorted, estimates):
- CON-001: Redirect service: implement mapping + 20 most-used redirects (Priority P0, 5d) -> JIRA: CONSOLE-8123
- CON-002: Hub Rail component + responsive behavior (P0, 8d) -> PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/458
- CON-003: Workspace Strip UI + context popovers (P1, 6d)
- CON-004: Telemetry schema + analytics dashboard (P1, 3d) -> linked to Analytics board
- CON-005: Role-aware visibility rules + policy testing (P1, 5d)
- CON-006: Mobile bottom-sheet hub implementation (P2, 5d)
- CON-007: Accessibility pass & keyboard test plan (P1, 2d)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we expose the workspace ID in the primary URL for single-tenant Private deployments? (security/obfuscation debate). Action: SRE/security to propose masked ID strategy by 2025-03-07.
- Which hubs are 'primary' on small orgs vs large orgs? Need telemetry threshold gating (e.g., show only 4 hubs if user has < 10 resources).
- How aggressive should legacy redirects be vs showing alias in nav? Tradeoffs: SEO, customer links, developer docs.

Notes from user testing (synthesized):
- New users often look for "where are my models" and land on Monitoring rather than Models. A hub-first label set reduced misclicks in prototype by ~32% (small N = 8).
- Power users disliked excessive nesting; adding workspace strip chips gave them a reliable anchor to jump between models and routes.

Next steps & immediate actions (owner: Asha):
- Ship redirect table for top 20 paths (CON-001) by 2025-03-08. Coordinate with Dev-Infra.
- Kick off Hub Rail UI engineering spike (Derek) — exploratory PR by 2025-03-14.
- Build telemetry events (Maya) and wire up a short dashboard to measure hub adoption week over week.
- Schedule cross-team review with SRE/security and DX to finalize URL contract.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a synthesis doc intended to capture tradeoffs and shape the P0/P1 backlog. Expect updates after the engineering spike and initial redirect rollout. Please comment inline or drop notes in Slack #console-ia with the prefix "IA:CONSOLE".

Rough sketches attached elsewhere: see linked PR for initial component screenshots and the Confluence page for full recording links.

-- Asha
